# 3 Maccabees Chapter 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** The Jews Imprisoned in the Hippodrome

---

**4:1** Wherever this decree reached, a festival was proclaimed among the Gentiles, with joyfulness and gladness, the hatred which had been so long kept hidden in their hearts now finding open expression.

**4:2** But among the Jews there was incessant mourning, lamentation, and tearful crying; their hearts were set ablaze with groaning as they mourned their unexpected reversal of fortune.

**4:3** What district or city or what habitable place or what streets were not filled with wailing and lamentation over them?

**4:4** They were sent out under such bitter and pitiless compulsion by the generals in the various cities that at the sight of their unusual punishments, even some of their enemies were moved to pity and reflected on the uncertainty of life, thinking that these same reversals might come upon themselves at any time.

**4:5** A host of old men with white hair were driven along with bent backs from the rough treatment they had received along the way, their legs bowed from old age and shame.

**4:6** Young women who had just entered the bridal chamber to share a life of wedded love, with veils over their faces in place of joy, and who had exchanged ointments of fragrance for unwashed hair, were driven along; and instead of wedding hymns they were escorted with wailing.

**4:7** They were dragged by force, while in bonds, in full view of all.

**4:8** In public and wretched disgrace they were thrust aboard the ships and brought with their children to Alexandria.

**4:9** When they arrived there, the king gave orders that they be concentrated in the hippodrome which was before the city.

**4:10** The place was enormous, and magnificently fitted for such a scene; it was suited to make them visible to all who came and went to the city and to all who went in to the royal palace.

**4:11** This was done out of complete malice, so that they who had been deprived of all their possessions would also be objects of scorn.

**4:12** And there, imprisoned as though they were criminals condemned to death, the Jews waited.

**4:13** Meanwhile there was Hermon, the elephant keeper, with his five hundred war elephants, and Ptolemy had ordered him to get the elephants drunk on unmixed wine mixed with frankincense and then to release them against the Jews in the early morning, so that they would be trampled underfoot.

**4:14** Thus the Jews, all herded together in the hippodrome, would be destroyed.

**4:15** But when the king had given these orders, his friends — seeing his extreme and groundless cruelty against the Jews — pleaded with him to cancel the order, saying:

**4:16** O king, do not act in this way! Do not bring ruin upon your kingdom by treating kindly people with such cruelty.

**4:17** But the king was filled with fury and paid no attention to their words.

**4:18** When morning came, the order had still not been carried out, and the guards reported to the king that the elephants had not been prepared.

**4:19** The king was greatly angered and threatened to punish Hermon and his men for this failure.

**4:20** But Hermon and his officials excused themselves, saying that the elephants had not been given the wine in time.

**4:21** The king therefore put off the punishment until the following day and gave the order again.

**4:22** All that day the assembled Jews in the hippodrome prayed to God with tears and lamentation.

**4:23** They called upon the Almighty Lord and Master of all power, their merciful God and Father, imploring him to turn aside the wicked plan that was being carried out against them.
